extracted.intended_audience: general literate public interested in education and public policy; especially workmen/parents and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Identify criteria for judging whether state-sponsored (compulsory, rate-supported) education helps or hinders social progress, liberty, justice, parental responsibility, and civic life. The page is an argumentative magazine essay giving normative standards and examples to evaluate state education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of justice and liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: Any institution (including state education) must answer whether it is founded on justice and whether it supports or undermines the liberty of men; these questions must come first and not be subordinated to appeals of usefulness or sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author insists answers be simple and straightforward; evaluate the institution by whether it preserves individual liberty within limits of like liberty for others. Anti-pattern: defending an institution solely by utility while ignoring justice and liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory funding creates dependence
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever one set of people pay (by rate or tax) for what another set uses, that payment is a favour and necessarily creates a form of dependence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether financing mechanisms force contributions from groups that do not directly use the service; consider resulting loss of independence. Example: workmen paying rates for schooling they do not control leads to dependence on the richer classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness of making one class pay for another's benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: It is unjust to make one set of men pay for what is used by another set; extracting money by legislation from richer classes to benefit poorer is morally questionable if taken by compulsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge funding arrangements by principles of distributive justice: does the system place burdens on others merely because they can bear them? Anti-pattern: treating fiscal extraction as legitimate because beneficiaries 'need' it without checking justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control and representation in governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Who directs education matters: the composition of boards (ministers, merchants, manufacturers, squires) shows that workmen often have little real voice in managing their children's education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate governance structures — presence/absence of meaningful representation for those whose children are educated. Look at school board composition and decision-making power. Anti-pattern: nominal representation that masks real control by wealthy/interested groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary versus obligatory provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary gifts and voluntary organization preserve moral equality and the grace of giving; forced contributions bring moral hurt to both giver and receiver and have evil consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer models that enable voluntary contributions and community-organized education. Examine whether the system crowds out voluntary efforts or replaces them with compulsion. Scoring note: voluntary systems score higher for fostering civic virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on parental responsibility and character formation
rubrics_metrics.description: State intrusion between parents and children removes the natural opportunities for forethought, self-denial, affection, and responsibility that form character; by making education someone else's duty, parents lose incentives to cultivate these virtues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the extent to which the education system reduces parental duties and opportunities for moral growth. Use historical parallels (e.g., poor laws reducing family care) as evidence of erosion of family obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper scope of state functions (legitimacy of state role)
rubrics_metrics.description: The state should confine itself to making arrangements necessary to secure liberty (e.g., civil/criminal law, defense) and abstain from interfering in religion and education, which properly belong to individuals and voluntary groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether education falls within duties the state legitimately must perform to secure equal liberty. Cite Herbert Spencer's view that state exists for liberty; assess whether the program exceeds that trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politicalization and partisan influence
rubrics_metrics.description: School boards and municipal educational administration become arenas for party politics where contests are fought on simple, familiar political issues (Sundays, women, rate-support), not on the institution's special educational principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate susceptibility to partisan battles and whether elections reduce educational governance to familiar political cleavages rather than institutional expertise. Anti-pattern: decisions driven by party lines rather than educational needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incompatibility of representative politics with complex institutional administration
rubrics_metrics.description: A representative chosen by a large and diverse electorate cannot adequately represent the varied and detailed convictions relevant to administering a large, complicated institution like education; representation forces suppression of differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess governance forms for their capacity to represent nuanced stakeholder views; prefer voluntary, like-with-like groupings for complex administration. Scoring: systems relying on single representatives for diverse views rate poorly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardization that ignores parental diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: State statutes make no distinctions between parents (good and bad) and assume with impartiality that every parent intends to defraud the child, imposing uniform legal obligations and inspections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the system enforces one-size-fits-all standards that disregard legitimate parental differences. Anti-pattern: blanket inspection and penalty regimes that presume parental untrustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on voluntary philanthropy and private endowment
rubrics_metrics.description: When opportunities for voluntary giving exist, wealthy classes give generously (endowments, support for schools, religious institutions); unwisely designed legislation can close these channels and reduce private philanthropy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the public system crowds out or preserves channels for voluntary endowments and charity. Positive signal: persistence/opportunity for private gifts; negative: legal structures that deter voluntary giving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erosion of social independence and increase of intolerance
rubrics_metrics.description: Political arrangements that force people to struggle against each other (man against man) breed mutual suspicion and intolerance; by contrast, cutting compulsory interference allows tolerant coexistence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess social effects: does the educational system increase competition/coercion among groups, or does it enable freedom of difference? Look for measures of civic tolerance and social friction as outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioning the asserted necessity of book-education
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim that book-education is a necessity of life (used to justify compulsion) is not strictly true; necessity claims must be examined before invoking compulsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand precise definitions and empirical support before accepting necessity as justification for compulsory provision; avoid using vague 'necessity' rhetoric to mandate funding or attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of voluntary organization for progress and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary organizations, where like attracts like and groups form around shared views, enable continual progress and the practical application of new ideas; political administration tends toward immobility and suppressed innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor institutional forms that allow voluntary grouping, experimentation, and local initiative. Scoring: systems that allow diversity of voluntary schools/associations score higher on responsiveness and innovation.
